title: Molecular windage of thermalized cascades
scope:
Molecular recirculation work in explicitly thermalized moving-blade cascades.
No new trajectories: uses archived cumulative work per open-mouth incident molecule.

inputs.moving_tip_scope: Both front and back flat tangentially moving faces cover fraction1-f. Their work is zero if specular; m u^2 per incidence if fully diffuse. Oblique edges/additional disk faces are not modeled.

equations.open_shaft: sum_i Ai f vbar/(4 kT) [pi Wf+pnext Wr]
equations.tips: sum_i Ai(1-f) vbar/(4 kT)(pi+pnext) m u^2 alpha_tip

limitations: Ideal isothermal stationary reset reservoirs must be physically implemented; their transmission losses are outside this row model.
All cumulative wall work within each row is already counted; do not multiply by reflection counts.
Motor electrical inputs must include molecular windage, bearing/drive losses and other exposed rotating surfaces. Do not add windage twice to a total-motor requirement.
Pressure-stage area reduction requires physical confinement of higher-pressure gas to smaller moving areas. Exposed annuli retain drag; tapering a flow aperture alone does not remove their windage.
Same local tip speed at each reduced area is assumed; preserve radius with reduced annular span or provide separate appropriate-speed rotors.
Mean local pressure calculation excludes thermalized pump internal storage relative to day-scale buffer response. Pulse-resolved local high-pressure transport may be collisional.
The mean-path collision diagnostic uses a stipulated effective area1e-19m2 and arithmetic mean adjacent pressure; it is not a Boltzmann collision calculation.

Archived records omit work variances/covariances. Independent discovery samples test numerical stability but do not provide a formal work uncertainty interval. Surface scattering, stator transmission and geometry dominate this epistemic uncertainty.
